findings.title: Full frontend test suite fails from broken ProductGallery/ProductVideo/ProductForm test setup
findings.environment: local workspace, frontend, Vitest v4.1.10, jsdom
preconditions: dependencies installed
current worktree as of 2026-07-29
reproduction_steps: Run cd frontend && npm test.
Run cd frontend && npx vitest run __tests__/components/products/ProductGallery.test.tsx __tests__/components/ProductVideo.test.tsx __tests__/components/admin/ProductForm.test.tsx --reporter=verbose.
findings.expected_result: Frontend regression suite passes or fails only on real product regressions.
evidence: npm test: 3 failed files, 8 failed tests, 35 passed files, 230 passed tests.
ProductGallery.test.tsx: 4 failures with TypeError: window.matchMedia is not a function at frontend/components/products/ProductGallery.tsx:38.
ProductVideo.test.tsx: 3 failures with missing NextIntlClientProvider at frontend/components/products/ProductGallery.tsx:28.
ProductForm.test.tsx: onSubmit remains uncalled; rendered form shows Could not load taxonomy. and Product type is required.
relevant_logs: Failed to call useTranslations because the context from NextIntlClientProvider was not found.
TypeError: window.matchMedia is not a function
expected vi.fn() to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
findings.likely_cause: Test setup lacks a global window.matchMedia shim, ProductVideo tests bypass the shared intl wrapper, and ProductForm tests use a product fixture/mocks that do not satisfy required taxonomy/product_type validation.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add global browser API shims, require translated component renders through the shared helper, and keep admin form fixtures/API mocks synchronized with required product fields.

findings.title: Updating an admin product drops existing video from the update response
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI client, ENVIRONMENT=development, admin bearer key
preconditions: product has an existing product_videos row with status='ready'
reproduction_steps: Seed product video-candle and a ready product_videos row for it.
GET /v1/admin/products/video-candle with a valid admin bearer token.
PATCH /v1/admin/products/video-candle with {"name_en":"Video Candle Updated"}.
GET /v1/admin/products/video-candle again.
findings.expected_result: The PATCH response includes the same video object as the GET responses because the product still has a video and the response model includes video.
findings.actual_result: The PATCH response returns video: null; both GET responses include the ready video object.
evidence: Before PATCH: GET returned video id video-1 for product video-candle.
PATCH response: status 200, name_en='Video Candle Updated', video=None.
After PATCH: GET returned the same ready video object, proving persistence was not removed.
app/services/product_service.py update_product() attaches image fields but not product_video_service.attach_video_fields_one(...).
relevant_logs: No backend error; API returns 200.
api_requests_responses: PATCH /v1/admin/products/video-candle {name_en: Video Candle Updated} -> 200 with video null
findings.likely_cause: update_product() ends with product_image_service.attach_image_fields_one(product) and does not attach video fields.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add a backend admin product update test that seeds a ready video, patches a non-video field, and asserts the update response still includes video.

findings.title: Route-level API errors omit the documented details field
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI client, ENVIRONMENT=development
preconditions: API app created from create_app()
admin bearer key configured for admin probes
reproduction_steps: Seed product dup-candle.
POST /v1/admin/products with duplicate id='dup-candle'.
POST /v1/admin/products with product_type='missing-type'.
GET /v1/admin/orders?status=bogus.
GET /v1/products/nope.
findings.expected_result: Every error follows the documented app envelope: {error:{code,message,details}}.
findings.actual_result: These route-created errors include code and message but omit details entirely.
evidence: Duplicate create: 409 {'error': {'code': 'DUPLICATE', 'message': 'Product with this ID already exists'}}, details missing.
Invalid taxonomy: 422 {'error': {'code': 'INVALID_TAXONOMY', 'message': 'Unknown product type: missing-type'}}, details missing.
Invalid admin order status: 422 {'error': {'code': 'INVALID_STATUS', 'message': "Invalid status 'bogus'. Must be one of: pending, confirmed, shipped, delivered, cancelled"}}, details missing.
Missing public product: 404 {'error': {'code': 'NOT_FOUND', 'message': 'Product not found'}}, details missing.
app/main.py documents all errors with details; app/exceptions.py global handlers include it.
relevant_logs: No backend error; responses are successful error responses.
findings.database_state: seed product dup-candle required for duplicate path
findings.likely_cause: Route handlers return handcrafted JSONResponse bodies instead of a shared error helper/global exception path, and many omit details.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add schema assertions for representative custom route errors and centralize error response construction so details is always present.

findings.title: Checkout summary line items show full price for discounted products while subtotal uses discounted total
findings.environment: local workspace, frontend checkout component, backend discount tests green
preconditions: cart contains a product with active discount fields, e.g. price_cents=3200 and effective_price_cents=2560
cart total_cents is computed from effective_price_cents, as backend and mock API do
reproduction_steps: Use a cart item whose product has price_cents=3200, effective_price_cents=2560, discount_percent=20, quantity=1, and cart total_cents=2560.
Render or inspect the checkout order summary in frontend/app/[locale]/checkout/page.tsx.
Compare the line item unit/line total with the subtotal.
findings.expected_result: The checkout summary line item uses the same effective discounted price as the cart subtotal, e.g. 1 x €25.60 and subtotal €25.60.
findings.actual_result: The line item uses product.price_cents, so it displays 1 x €32.00 and line total €32.00 while the subtotal displays €25.60 from total_cents.
findings.reproduction_rate: 1/1 code-path inspection against the active checkout component plus passing backend discount contract tests
evidence: frontend/app/[locale]/checkout/page.tsx lines 287 and 291 format item.product.price_cents instead of item.product.effective_price_cents.
frontend/lib/mock-api.ts buildCartResponse computes total_cents from item.product.effective_price_cents.
tests/test_discounts.py::TestCartTotals::test_cart_total_uses_effective_price and TestCheckoutSnapshot::test_checkout_snapshots_discounted_price passed in the focused tests/test_discounts.py run.
Mock discounted product lavender-dreams-300ml has price_cents=3200 and effective_price_cents=2560.
relevant_logs: .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_discounts.py -q -> 19 passed
findings.likely_cause: Checkout summary uses the base ProductResponse.price_cents field for display math instead of the discounted ProductResponse.effective_price_cents field used by cart totals and order snapshots.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add a checkout page/component test with a discounted cart item and assert the unit price, line total, and subtotal all use effective_price_cents.

findings.title: Client-side product price sorting ignores active discounts
findings.environment: local workspace, frontend ProductListingClient, backend discount tests green
preconditions: product list contains at least one discounted product whose effective_price_cents changes its ordering relative to base price
user selects price ascending or price descending in the product menu
reproduction_steps: Use products sale-candle price_cents=5000 effective_price_cents=1000 and plain-candle price_cents=2000 effective_price_cents=2000.
Apply the client price_asc sort from ProductListingClient.
Compare the result to the backend/public contract that sorts by effective_price_cents.
findings.expected_result: price_asc orders sale-candle before plain-candle because 1000 < 2000, matching backend effective-price sorting and the displayed sale prices.
findings.actual_result: price_asc orders plain-candle before sale-candle because the client sorts by base price_cents, 2000 < 5000.
findings.reproduction_rate: 1/1 direct executable sort probe plus code inspection
evidence: Executable probe output: client_price_asc=[plain-candle,sale-candle], expected_effective_price_asc=[sale-candle,plain-candle].
frontend/components/products/ProductListingClient.tsx lines 211-215 sort price_asc/price_desc by price_cents.
app/services/product_service.py lines 218-260 documents and implements price sort by effective_price_cents.
tests/test_discounts.py::TestPriceSort::test_price_asc_uses_effective_price and test_price_desc_uses_effective_price passed in the focused tests/test_discounts.py run.
relevant_logs: node probe -> {"client_price_asc":["plain-candle","sale-candle"],"expected_effective_price_asc":["sale-candle","plain-candle"]}
.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_discounts.py -q -> 19 passed

findings.title: Returning OAuth login clears stored name and avatar when Google omits optional claims
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, direct auth_service.upsert_user probe
preconditions: A user already exists with google_id, name, and avatar_url populated.
A later OAuth callback for the same google_id provides no name and no picture claim.
reproduction_steps: Initialize a temp DB and call auth_service.upsert_user(conn, google-1, a@test.com, Old Name, http://old-avatar.jpg).
Call auth_service.upsert_user(conn, google-1, a@test.com, None, None) for the same google_id.
Read SELECT id, name, avatar_url FROM users WHERE google_id = google-1.
findings.expected_result: The stored profile keeps the previous non-null name and avatar when the provider omits optional replacement values, or the returned UserResponse matches what was actually persisted.
findings.actual_result: The returned UserResponse still reports Old Name and http://old-avatar.jpg, but the users table row is updated to name=NULL and avatar_url=NULL.
evidence: Probe output second_return={'name':'Old Name','avatar_url':'http://old-avatar.jpg'} while db_row={'name': None, 'avatar_url': None}.
app/services/auth_service.py lines 343-345 update name and avatar_url directly from nullable OAuth claims.
app/services/auth_service.py lines 350-351 return fallback values from the old row, masking the persisted nulls in the immediate response.
Existing TestUpsertUser only covers returning users with replacement name/avatar, not omitted optional claims.
relevant_logs: .venv/bin/python direct probe -> db_row {'name': None, 'avatar_url': None} after second upsert
findings.database_state: users row for google-1 changed from name=Old Name/avatar_url=http://old-avatar.jpg to name=NULL/avatar_url=NULL
findings.likely_cause: The returning-user update writes nullable name/avatar_url values directly, but the response object falls back to the previous values instead of reflecting the database mutation.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add an upsert_user test for an existing user where name and avatar_url are omitted, asserting the stored row preserves existing non-null values or the response and persistence are intentionally aligned.

findings.title: Admin bank-transfer payment confirmation queues duplicate placed email rows
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI admin route probe, ENVIRONMENT=development, admin bearer key
preconditions: An order exists with payment_method=bank_transfer and payment_status=pending.
The admin calls PATCH /v1/admin/orders/{order_id}/payment with payment_status=paid.
reproduction_steps: Create a bank_transfer checkout order in an isolated temp DB.
Before marking paid, query order_emails for that order.
PATCH /v1/admin/orders/{order_id}/payment with a valid admin bearer token and {payment_status: paid}.
After the route returns 200, query order_emails for that order again.
findings.expected_result: Exactly one queued placed email intent exists after payment is marked paid.
findings.actual_result: Two queued placed rows exist for the same order and recipient after the route returns 200.
evidence: Probe before: [{'event':'payment_pending','status':'queued'}, {'event':'admin_new_order','status':'queued'}].
Probe after: payment_pending queued, admin_new_order queued, plus two {'event':'placed','status':'queued','recipient':'test@example.com'} rows.
app/services/order_service.py lines 745-748 insert a queued placed row inside mark_bank_transfer_paid().
app/routes/admin.py lines 720-721 queues placed again after mark_bank_transfer_paid() returns.
app/database.py lines 263-265 only enforce uniqueness for status=sent, so duplicate queued rows are allowed.
relevant_logs: PATCH /v1/admin/orders/{order_id}/payment -> 200 with payment_status=paid
DB after route -> two queued placed rows for test@example.com
findings.database_state: order_emails contains duplicate queued placed rows for the same order_id/event/recipient after the admin payment route.
findings.likely_cause: Both the service layer and the admin route enqueue the same placed email intent, and queued outbox rows are not deduplicated by schema or helper.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add a route-level bank-transfer payment test that asserts a single placed row exists after PATCH /v1/admin/orders/{id}/payment; keep the enqueue responsibility in one layer or make queue_order_email idempotent for queued intents.

findings.title: Admin order payment status filter accepts invalid values as empty results
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI admin route probe, ENVIRONMENT=development, admin bearer key
preconditions: Admin bearer authentication is configured; no order data is required to reproduce the validation difference.
reproduction_steps: Start the app against a fresh temp SQLite DB with ADMIN_API_KEY=test-admin-key-realapp.
Send GET /v1/admin/orders?status=bogus with the admin bearer token.
Send GET /v1/admin/orders?payment_status=bogus with the same token.
Send GET /v1/admin/orders?payment_status=paid as a valid control.
findings.expected_result: Invalid payment_status should be rejected with a validation error, matching invalid status behavior and the PaymentStatus enum.
findings.actual_result: payment_status=bogus returns 200 with an empty page, indistinguishable from a valid filter that simply has no matching orders.
evidence: Probe output: /v1/admin/orders?status=bogus -> 422 {'error': {'code': 'INVALID_STATUS', ...}}.
Probe output: /v1/admin/orders?payment_status=bogus -> 200 {'items': [], 'total': 0, 'page': 1, 'limit': 20}.
Probe output: /v1/admin/orders?payment_status=paid -> 200 {'items': [], 'total': 0, 'page': 1, 'limit': 20}.
app/models/orders.py:11 defines PaymentStatus = Literal["pending", "paid", "cod_pending", "failed", "refunded"].
app/routes/admin.py lines 647-661 validate status, but lines 663-666 pass raw payment_status into the service.
app/services/order_service.py lines 575-602 accept payment_status: str | None and build WHERE payment_status = ? without enum validation.
relevant_logs: Local probe logged courier office data loading; no backend error was emitted for the invalid payment status.
findings.database_state: fresh DB with no orders; the bug is visible before any records exist because it is a request validation issue
findings.likely_cause: admin_list_orders() validates the status query parameter against OrderStatus but does not perform equivalent validation for payment_status against PaymentStatus.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add an admin order list route test for payment_status=bogus asserting a 422 error and another valid payment-status control asserting 200.

findings.title: Stripe retry endpoint accepts form posts and creates a new checkout session
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI route probe, fake Stripe module, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_probe
preconditions: A card order belongs to the current session and has payment_status='failed'.
Stripe is configured; the caller has the session cookie.
reproduction_steps: Seed a session, product, cart item, and card order in a fresh temp SQLite DB.
Set the order to payment_status='failed' and stripe_checkout_session_id='cs_old'.
Install a fake local stripe.checkout.Session.create returning id='cs_form_retry' and url='https://stripe.test/retry'.
Send POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/stripe-session with the session cookie, body x=1, and Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded.
Read the order's stripe_checkout_session_id from the database.
findings.expected_result: State-changing order/payment endpoints should reject form-encoded POSTs with the same content-type guard used by POST /v1/orders, or otherwise enforce an equivalent CSRF-safe request contract.
findings.actual_result: The retry endpoint returns 200 with a stripe_checkout_url, calls stripe.checkout.Session.create once, and updates the order row to stripe_checkout_session_id='cs_form_retry'.
evidence: Probe output: response 200 {'stripe_checkout_url': 'https://stripe.test/retry'}.
Probe output: db {'payment_status': 'failed', 'stripe_checkout_session_id': 'cs_form_retry'}.
Probe output: stripe_calls 1.
app/routes/orders.py lines 51-60 enforce Content-Type: application/json for checkout POSTs.
app/routes/orders.py lines 169-222 implement the Stripe retry POST without reading Request or enforcing content type.
tests/realapp/test_order_routes.py lines 463-492 cover form-encoded rejection only for POST /v1/orders.
relevant_logs: Local probe logged courier office data loading; no backend error was emitted.
api_requests_responses: POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/stripe-session with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded and body x=1 -> 200 with stripe_checkout_url
findings.database_state: order remained payment_status='failed', but stripe_checkout_session_id changed from cs_old to cs_form_retry
findings.likely_cause: create_stripe_retry_session() is a cookie-authenticated state-changing POST but lacks the content-type/CSRF guard present on create_order().
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add a route-level test that posts form-encoded content to /v1/orders/{id}/stripe-session with a retryable card order and asserts a 422 INVALID_CONTENT_TYPE response and no Stripe call/session-id mutation.

findings.title: User avatar fallback renders blank when profile name is an empty string
findings.environment: local workspace, direct backend auth service probe plus executable frontend fallback-expression probe
preconditions: An authenticated user has name='' and avatar_url=null, or their avatar image fails and name='' is present in the user response.
reproduction_steps: Create or upsert a user through auth_service.upsert_user(conn, 'google-empty-name', 'empty@example.com', '', None).
Observe that the backend UserResponse and database row preserve name='' and avatar_url=None.
Evaluate the UserAvatar fallback expression with name='' and email='empty@example.com'.
Compare it with the same expression for name=null.
findings.expected_result: When the display name is blank, the avatar fallback should use the email initial, E, just as it does when name is null.
findings.actual_result: name='' produces an empty string initial with length 0, so the circular fallback avatar renders with no visible character.
findings.reproduction_rate: 1/1 backend state probe and 1/1 frontend expression probe
evidence: Backend probe output: response {'email': 'empty@example.com', 'name': '', 'avatar_url': None, ...} and db_row {'email': 'empty@example.com', 'name': '', 'avatar_url': None}.
Frontend expression probe output: {"name":"","email":"empty@example.com","initial":"","initialLength":0}.
Control output: {"name":null,"email":"empty@example.com","initial":"E","initialLength":1}.
frontend/components/auth/UserAvatar.tsx:34 computes name?.charAt(0).toUpperCase() ?? email.charAt(0).toUpperCase(), so empty string short-circuits the nullish fallback.
frontend/components/auth/UserAvatar.tsx lines 53-58 render {initial} directly inside the fallback circle.
frontend/__tests__/components/auth/UserMenu.test.tsx lines 128-154 cover avatar_url=null with name='Marie', but not blank names.
relevant_logs: No backend error; the probes returned successfully.
findings.database_state: users row for google-empty-name has name='' and avatar_url=NULL
findings.likely_cause: The avatar fallback treats only null/undefined names as absent and does not trim or test for a non-empty display name before deriving the initial.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add a UserAvatar or UserMenu test where name='' and avatar_url=null, asserting the email initial is rendered; normalize blank names before computing initials.

findings.title: Authenticated user menu button has no descriptive accessible name
findings.environment: local workspace, source inspection plus dom-accessibility-api accessible-name probe
preconditions: The header renders an authenticated user with avatar_url present, or the avatar falls back to a single initial.
reproduction_steps: Inspect UserMenu rendered inside the authenticated header.
For the image-avatar state, compute the accessible name of a button with aria-expanded='false', aria-haspopup='menu', and an inner .
For the fallback state, compute the accessible name of the same button with an inner M.
findings.expected_result: The menu trigger has a stable descriptive accessible name such as Account menu, User menu, or localized equivalent in both image and fallback states.
findings.actual_result: The image-avatar state has an empty accessible name, and the fallback state is named only M.
evidence: Accessible-name probe output: {"imageButtonName":"","imageButtonNameLength":0}.
Accessible-name probe output: {"fallbackButtonName":"M","fallbackButtonNameLength":1}.
frontend/components/auth/UserMenu.tsx lines 57-67 render the trigger button with aria-expanded and aria-haspopup, but no aria-label or visible descriptive text.
frontend/components/auth/UserAvatar.tsx:31 defaults alt='', and lines 42-49 render the loaded avatar image as decorative.
frontend/components/layout/Header.tsx lines 80-83 show the nearby cart button has an explicit aria-label, so this is inconsistent within the same header controls.
frontend/__tests__/components/auth/UserMenu.test.tsx lines 114-124 assert ARIA expanded/menu attributes but do not assert an accessible name.

findings.title: Admin CSV import crashes on invalid UTF-8 upload instead of returning CSV validation error
findings.area: Backend / API / Admin Products / CSV Import
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI admin route probe, raise_app_exceptions true and false controls
preconditions: Admin bearer authentication is configured; upload a .csv file whose bytes are not valid UTF-8.
reproduction_steps: Start the app against a fresh temp SQLite DB with ADMIN_API_KEY=test-admin-key-realapp.
Send POST /v1/admin/products/import as admin with multipart file bad.csv, content bytes b'\xff\xfe\x00\x00', and content type text/csv.
Run once with ASGI raise_app_exceptions=False to observe the HTTP response.
Run once with ASGI raise_app_exceptions=True to observe the underlying exception.
findings.expected_result: Malformed or non-UTF-8 CSV uploads should return a controlled 400 INVALID_CSV style response without an unhandled exception stack trace.
findings.actual_result: The endpoint raises UnicodeDecodeError; with app exceptions suppressed, the client receives 500 {"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"An unexpected error occurred","details":null}}.
evidence: HTTP probe output: raise_false 500 {"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"An unexpected error occurred","details":null}}.
Exception probe output: raise_true_exception UnicodeDecodeError 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte.
Logged stack trace points to app/routes/admin.py:407, text = content.decode("utf-8-sig").
app/routes/admin.py lines 395-407 read bounded upload bytes and decode directly without catching UnicodeDecodeError.
The route already maps oversize/missing-header/missing-column CSV cases to INVALID_CSV, so malformed encoding is inconsistent with adjacent validation behavior.
relevant_logs: Backend logs Unhandled exception on POST /v1/admin/products/import followed by a UnicodeDecodeError stack trace.
api_requests_responses: POST /v1/admin/products/import with invalid UTF-8 multipart CSV -> 500 INTERNAL_ERROR
findings.database_state: fresh DB; no product writes are required to reproduce
findings.likely_cause: admin_import_products() decodes uploaded bytes with content.decode('utf-8-sig') outside a validation try/except, so malformed encodings escape to the global 500 handler.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add a route test uploading invalid UTF-8 bytes to /v1/admin/products/import and assert a controlled 400 INVALID_CSV response with no product writes.

findings.title: CSV import reports success while silently dropping image_url when gallery is full
findings.area: Backend / API / Admin Products / CSV Import
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI admin route probe, product pre-seeded with six image rows
preconditions: An existing product already has six product_images rows; a CSV import row for that product includes a new image_url.
reproduction_steps: Seed product full-gallery and six existing product_images rows for it.
Upload CSV id,name_en,price_cents,image_url\nfull-gallery,Full Gallery Updated,2500,/static/products/new-image.webp\n through POST /v1/admin/products/import as admin.
Read the API response.
Query product_images for full-gallery and check whether /static/products/new-image.webp was added.
findings.expected_result: If the supplied image_url cannot be attached because the gallery is full, the import should report a row error or otherwise communicate that the image was skipped.
findings.actual_result: The API returns 200 {'created': 0, 'updated': 1, 'errors': []} and updates the product text/price, but the submitted image URL is absent from product_images.
evidence: Probe response: response 200 {'created': 0, 'updated': 1, 'errors': []}.
DB product row after import: {'name_en': 'Full Gallery Updated', 'price_cents': 2500}.
DB image state after import: image_count 6, has_new_image False.
Existing image URLs remained ['/static/products/full-0.webp', ..., '/static/products/full-5.webp'].
app/services/product_image_service.py lines 257-278 return None when current['count'] >= MAX_IMAGES_PER_PRODUCT.
app/routes/admin.py lines 617-624 ignore the return value from add_existing_image_url() and increment updated/created without adding an error.
relevant_logs: No backend error; the row is treated as successful.
api_requests_responses: POST /v1/admin/products/import with a valid CSV row including image_url for a full-gallery product -> 200, updated=1, errors=[]
findings.database_state: product fields changed, image count stayed at six, and the submitted image URL was not persisted
findings.likely_cause: add_existing_image_url() uses None as a max-images sentinel, but admin_import_products() treats any non-exception return as success and does not check for None.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add a CSV import test for an existing product with six images and an image_url, asserting the row reports an error or a skipped-image status and does not claim an unqualified success.

findings.title: Public comments display HTML entities literally for normal punctuation
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI client, React server-rendering probe using frontend dependencies
preconditions: an active product exists
a user posts a comment or display name containing normal escapable characters such as &, <, >, or quotes
reproduction_steps: Seed active product entity-candle in an isolated temp SQLite DB.
POST /v1/products/entity-candle/comments with {"display_name":"Tom & Jerry","body":"I use <this> & \"that\""}.
GET /v1/products/entity-candle/comments and GET /v1/admin/comments.
Render returned strings as React text children, matching frontend/components/products/CommentCard.tsx.
findings.expected_result: Public and admin comment surfaces display the user's text as entered, for example Tom & Jerry and I use <this> & "that", while still preventing HTML execution.
findings.actual_result: The API stores and returns escaped entity strings. React escapes those strings again as text children, so the visible UI shows literal entity text such as & instead of &.
findings.reproduction_rate: 1/1 isolated ASGI probe plus 1/1 React rendering probe
evidence: POST response: 201 {'display_name': 'Tom & Jerry', 'body': 'I use <this> & "that"', ...}.
Public list response returns the same escaped display_name and body.
Admin list response returns the same escaped display_name and body.
DB row: {'display_name': 'Tom & Jerry', 'body': 'I use <this> & "that"'}.

React rendering probe: renderToStaticMarkup(

{'Tom & Jerry'}

) produced

Tom & Jerry

.
frontend/components/products/CommentCard.tsx renders comment.display_name and comment.body as normal React text children.
app/services/comment_service.py calls sanitize_text() before insert, and app/utils/sanitize.py implements it with html.escape(text, quote=True).
relevant_logs: No backend error; courier office startup logs appeared during local app creation.
api_requests_responses: POST /v1/products/entity-candle/comments with JSON body containing &, <, and quotes -> 201 containing escaped entities
findings.database_state: comments.display_name and comments.body persist entity-escaped strings rather than the original text
findings.likely_cause: The backend uses HTML entity encoding as storage-level sanitization, but the frontend consumes API strings as plain text and relies on React escaping, causing double-escaping at render time.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add an API/comment UI integration test that posts text containing &, <, and quotes, then asserts rendered text matches the original plain text while markup remains inert.

findings.title: Contact form newline names create multiline owner-email subjects
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI client, direct contact email drain with recording provider
preconditions: contact form endpoint is available
owner contact email drain processes queued contact messages
reproduction_steps: Initialize an isolated temp SQLite DB and app.
POST /v1/contact with {"name":"Ava\nBcc: victim@example.com","email":"ava@example.com","message":"Can I order a custom candle?","locale":"en"}.
Query contact_messages for the stored name and email status.
Run drain_contact_message_emails() with a recording email provider.
Inspect the provider call subject.
findings.expected_result: Public contact text that is reused in email header-like fields should reject or normalize line breaks before the message is accepted or before the email subject is rendered.
findings.actual_result: The submission is accepted with 201, the name is persisted with an embedded newline, and the owner email subject becomes New contact message from Ava\nBcc: victim@example.com.
evidence: Contact POST response: 201 {'status': 'received', 'message_id': 1}.
DB row after POST: {'name': 'Ava\nBcc: victim@example.com', 'email_status': 'queued'}.
Drain result: processed 1; contact row changed to email_status='sent', email_attempts=1.
Recording provider subject: 'New contact message from Ava\nBcc: victim@example.com'.
Email body also starts a new line in the Name field: ['Name: Ava', 'Bcc: victim@example.com', ...].
Python stdlib header check rejects the same value: ValueError Header values may not contain linefeed or carriage return characters.
app/models/contact.py trims leading/trailing whitespace but does not reject internal CR/LF in name.
app/email/templates/en/contact_message.txt places {{ submitter_name }} on the subject line.
relevant_logs: local app startup logged courier office data loads; drain logged contact_email_sent for the contact message
api_requests_responses: POST /v1/contact with newline-containing name -> 201 and queued contact message
findings.database_state: contact_messages.name persists the embedded newline, and the message is marked sent after drain with the malformed subject passed to the provider
findings.likely_cause: Contact validation only strips outer whitespace and the plain-text email template renders untrusted submitter_name directly into the first-line subject.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add contact route/email rendering coverage for CR/LF in name, asserting the API rejects it with validation or normalizes it before rendering the owner email subject.

findings.title: FAQ reorder accepts duplicate IDs and creates duplicate sort_order values
findings.area: Backend / API / Admin FAQ / Data Integrity
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI admin route probe, seeded FAQ data
preconditions: FAQ section care has at least three items
admin bearer authentication is configured
reproduction_steps: Initialize an isolated temp SQLite DB and app.
GET /v1/admin/faq as admin and collect the first three care item IDs, observed as [7, 8, 9].
PATCH /v1/admin/faq/reorder with {"section":"care","ordered_ids":[7,7,8]}.
Read the response and query faq_items for section=care ordered by sort_order, id.
findings.expected_result: Reorder should reject duplicate item IDs with a validation error and leave existing FAQ order unchanged.
findings.actual_result: The route returns 200; item 7 is updated twice and ends at sort_order=1, item 8 gets sort_order=2, and omitted existing item 9 still has sort_order=2, leaving two items in the same section with the same order value.
evidence: Initial care IDs: [7, 8, 9].
Reorder response status: 200.
Response first care items after reorder: [(7, 1), (8, 2), (9, 2), (10, 3), (11, 4)].
DB first care rows after reorder: [{id: 7, sort_order: 1}, {id: 8, sort_order: 2}, {id: 9, sort_order: 2}, ...].
Duplicate sort-order query: [{sort_order: 2, c: 2}].
app/services/faq_service.py checks for missing and wrong-section IDs but does not check ordered_ids uniqueness before enumerating updates.
app/database.py has only idx_faq_items_section_order on (section, sort_order), not a uniqueness constraint, so duplicate positions persist.
relevant_logs: No backend error; local app startup logged courier office data loads.
api_requests_responses: PATCH /v1/admin/faq/reorder {"section":"care","ordered_ids":[7,7,8]} -> 200 with duplicate sort_order values in the returned section
findings.database_state: faq_items for care contains duplicate sort_order=2 after the request
findings.likely_cause: reorder_items() treats the input list as trusted after existence checks; duplicate IDs collapse in the found map but still drive multiple update iterations, while omitted items keep their prior sort positions.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add an admin FAQ reorder test with duplicate IDs, asserting 422 INVALID_FAQ and no faq_items.sort_order changes.

frontend/components/atelier/AtelierSections.tsx renders section.heading, section.subheading, and item text as normal React text children.
frontend/components/atelier/BodyRenderer.tsx renders body blocks as normal React text children.
app/services/about_service.py sanitizes editable text with sanitize_text() before persistence.
tests/test_about_service.py::test_sanitization_escapes_html_on_write asserts escaped storage but does not verify rendered output.
relevant_logs: No backend error; local app startup logged courier office data loads.
api_requests_responses: PATCH /v1/admin/about/sections/hero with escapable characters -> 200 containing entity-escaped fields
findings.database_state: about_sections.heading_en and about_sections.subheading_en persist entity-escaped strings rather than the original admin text
findings.likely_cause: The about service uses HTML entity encoding as storage-level sanitization, but the public React page renders API strings as plain text and relies on React's escaping, causing double-escaping at display time.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add an about admin/public rendering test that edits heading/body text containing &, <, and quotes, then asserts the rendered atelier page displays the original characters as inert plain text.

findings.title: Checkout accepts and persists nonexistent courier office IDs
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, local ASGI client, seeded cart and product, courier office catalogue loaded from local JSON
preconditions: session cart contains at least one active product
customer selects office delivery
reproduction_steps: Initialize an isolated temp SQLite DB and app.
Seed product delivery-test-candle, a session, and one cart item.
POST /v1/orders with office delivery payload courier=econt, office_id=not-a-real-econt-office, office_name=Injected Office Name, office_type=apt, and a valid phone.
GET /v1/orders/{order_id} with the same session.
Query the Econt Sofia office catalogue for not-a-real-econt-office.
findings.expected_result: Checkout should reject an office delivery selection whose office_id does not exist for the selected courier, or at minimum resolve the server-side office record instead of trusting client-supplied office metadata.
findings.actual_result: Checkout returns 201, persists the fake office ID/name/type, and the order detail returns the same fake office data. The local Econt Sofia catalogue has 132 offices and does not contain not-a-real-econt-office.
findings.reproduction_rate: 1/1 isolated ASGI route probe plus 1/1 catalogue check
evidence: Checkout response status: 201.
Checkout response delivery details: {'courier': 'econt', 'office_id': 'not-a-real-econt-office', 'office_name': 'Injected Office Name', 'office_type': 'apt', 'phone': '+359888123456'}.
GET order response returns the same delivery_method='office', delivery_courier='econt', and fake delivery_details.
DB order row stores delivery_details JSON containing not-a-real-econt-office and Injected Office Name.
Catalogue check: econt_sofia_count 132, fake_id_present False, sample IDs were ['econt-48485', 'econt-1029', 'econt-48128', ...].
app/models/delivery.py validates only shape/literals/phone for DeliveryOffice; it does not validate office_id against delivery_service data.
app/services/order_service.py serializes delivery.office.model_dump() directly into orders.delivery_details.
relevant_logs: No backend error; local app startup logged courier office data loads.
api_requests_responses: GET /v1/orders/{order_id} -> 200 returning the same fake office delivery details
findings.database_state: orders.delivery_method='office', orders.delivery_courier='econt', and orders.delivery_details contains client-supplied nonexistent office metadata
findings.likely_cause: Checkout treats the frontend's selected office object as trusted input and does not resolve or verify it against the backend courier office catalogue before creating the order.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add checkout route coverage for nonexistent and courier-mismatched office_id values, asserting a validation error and no order/cart mutation.

findings.title: Stripe completion trusts order IDs and mutates cancelled or non-card orders
findings.environment: isolated temp SQLite DB, direct payment-service webhook handler probe
preconditions: a valid Stripe checkout.session.completed webhook references an existing order ID that is not currently payable, such as a cancelled card order or a COD order
reproduction_steps: Initialize an isolated temp SQLite DB.

Insert session s-card and order order-cancelled-card with status='cancelled', payment_method='card', payment_status='failed', stripe_checkout_session_id='cs_old', and customer email paid-late@example.com.
Call handle_payment_succeeded(conn, 'evt_cancelled_completed', 'order-cancelled-card', 'pi_cancelled', now), matching the service used by POST /v1/webhooks/stripe for checkout.session.completed.
Query the order, order_emails, and stripe_events.
Repeat with pending COD order order-cod-stripe (payment_method='cod', payment_status='cod_pending') and event evt_cod_completed.
findings.expected_result: A completed payment webhook should only mark an order paid when the order is a payable card order and the event matches the current Stripe checkout session; terminal cancelled orders and non-card orders should not receive Stripe payment success side effects.
findings.actual_result: The handler returns True, applies payment_status='paid', stores the Stripe payment intent, records the Stripe event, and queues a placed customer email for both a cancelled card order and a COD order.
evidence: Before handler: {'status': 'cancelled', 'payment_method': 'card', 'payment_status': 'failed', 'stripe_payment_intent_id': None}.
Handler result: True.
After handler: {'status': 'cancelled', 'payment_method': 'card', 'payment_status': 'paid', 'stripe_payment_intent_id': 'pi_cancelled'}.
Queued emails: [{'event': 'placed', 'recipient': 'paid-late@example.com', 'status': 'queued'}].
Stripe event row: {'event_id': 'evt_cancelled_completed', 'order_id': 'order-cancelled-card', 'event_type': 'checkout.session.completed'}.
COD before handler: {'status': 'pending', 'payment_method': 'cod', 'payment_status': 'cod_pending', 'stripe_payment_intent_id': None}.
COD after handler: {'status': 'pending', 'payment_method': 'cod', 'payment_status': 'paid', 'stripe_payment_intent_id': 'pi_cod'}.
COD queued emails: [{'event': 'placed', 'recipient': 'cod-stripe@example.com', 'status': 'queued'}].
app/routes/webhooks.py passes valid checkout.session.completed events directly to handle_payment_succeeded().

app/services/payment_service.py updates orders.payment_status='paid' by id only and queues placed email when an order row exists; it does not check orders.status, previous payment_status, payment_method, or current stripe_checkout_session_id.
relevant_logs: service logged stripe_payment_succeeded event_id=evt_cancelled_completed order_id=order-cancelled-card and stripe_payment_succeeded event_id=evt_cod_completed order_id=order-cod-stripe
api_requests_responses: Route-level path is POST /v1/webhooks/stripe with a valid Stripe-signed checkout.session.completed event whose client_reference_id is the affected order ID; direct service probes exercised the same handler branch without external Stripe signing.
findings.database_state: cancelled card probe leaves orders.status='cancelled' while changing orders.payment_status to paid; COD probe leaves payment_method='cod' while changing payment_status to paid; both probes queue placed emails and store Stripe events as processed
findings.likely_cause: handle_payment_succeeded() is idempotent by event ID but not state-aware; it applies payment success side effects to any existing order ID regardless of order status, payment method, previous payment status, or matching checkout session.
findings.regression_test_recommendation: Add payment webhook/service coverage for checkout.session.completed on cancelled, non-pending, and non-card orders, asserting no paid transition or placed email is queued unless the order is a payable card order and the session ID matches the current checkout session.
